entities.summary: Margaret of Lorraine, Duchess of Alençon, was a French noblewoman and a nun of the order of Poor Clares. Born into the Lorraine duchy around 1480, she rose to prominence as a pious and influential figure in Western Europe. Her life was marked by her dedication to her faith and her family, which included her husband, Louis I, Duke of Alençon, and their children. She was particularly devoted to her role as Duchess of Alençon, using her position to support the Poor Clares and promote the Catholic Church's interests. Margaret's legacy extends beyond her own lifetime, as she played a significant role in shaping the cultural and religious landscape of the region. She was beatified in 1921, a testament to her enduring devotion to her faith and her community. In the centuries following her death, her reputation as a model of piety and leadership has endured, inspiring generations of women and clergy alike.
